summary.text: 休 is commonly explained as a person resting beside a tree, matching its familiar sense “rest.” A competing interpretation reads the right-hand element as military marker posts and connects the graph with commendation; its original motivation remains disputed.

formation.text: The common analysis treats 休 as a semantic compound: 人 depicts a person and 木 a tree, together forming a scene of resting in its shade. Some early forms are interpreted as showing the tree top bending toward the person. A competing analysis identifies the right-hand element as 禾-like marker posts and connects the graph with recognition of military merit.

components.text: In the person-and-tree analysis, 人 depicts the person leaning toward the tree. The competing account disputes this reading of the whole graph but does not offer a different account of this element.

木 depicts the tree in the common analysis; some early forms are interpreted as bending its top toward the person to suggest shade. This account distinguishes it from 禾 despite a resemblance in some forms. The competing marker-post interpretation disputes this identification.

history.text: Catalog records list 休 among oracle-bone and bronze examples and in the seal-script category. They do not establish a sequence of graphic changes here.

The transmitted Shuowen explanation defines 休 as “cease; rest” and analyzes it as a person relying on a tree. A competing account instead proposes 禾-like paired markers at a military gate. These are interpretations of the graph, and the disagreement remains unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The common person-and-tree interpretation and the military marker-post interpretation disagree about the right-hand element and the graph’s original motivation; neither account resolves the dispute.
The cited bronze and received-text uses have no securely established order here, so the earliest lexical sense cannot be ranked confidently.

senses.text: Rest is supported by received-text examples and the transmitted Shuowen definition, but the earliest attested sense cannot be ranked securely.
休 is used with the meaning “stop” or “cease.” The cited examples do not show when this use arose relative to “rest.”
A proposed connection links resting in shade with shelter or protection. The cited uses do not establish the chronology or each step in that development.
Reported inscriptional uses include favor or reward. Their relation to rest or shelter is uncertain.
A competing graph analysis cites a bronze use glossed “good” or “commendable” and connects it with recognition of merit. This use does not settle the graph’s origin or the sense’s chronology.
The common current meaning includes resting or taking a break.

developments.text: Both meanings are attested, but the available evidence does not show that one developed from the other.

limitations.text: The earliest lexical sense cannot be securely ranked. Proposed links among shade, protection, favor, reward, goodness, pleasure, rest, and stopping do not establish a proven sequence.

overview.text: 休 is commonly explained as a person resting by a tree: 人 and 木 form a scene. Another interpretation reads the right side as military marker posts, so the graph’s original motivation remains uncertain.

components.text: 人 depicts the person in the common person-and-tree scene.
木 depicts the tree in the common analysis; the marker-post interpretation disputes this identification.

relationships.text: In the common person-and-tree interpretation, 人 depicts the person in the scene represented by 休.
In the common analysis, 木 depicts the tree beside which the person rests; the marker-post interpretation disputes this identification.
